Once upon a time Granny and Grandpa lived in a little house at the edge of a wood.
They had no children, and they were often lonely.
One morning Granny made a gingerbread man.
She gave him two raisin eyes, a smiling mouth and three candy buttons.
Then she laid him on a tray by the window.
After a while Granny came back to the tray, and she could not believe her eyes.
Up jumped the Gingerbread Man!
He blinked and waved.
Oh my!
said Granny.
Grandpa, come and see!
The Gingerbread Man hopped off the tray and ran across the kitchen floor.
Running was such fun!
Stop!
Come back and give me a cuddle!
Run, run, as fast as you can! You can't catch me, I'm the Gingerbread Man!
said Gingerbread Man.
Out of the door and down the lane he ran.
Granny and Grandpa hurried after him, puffing and laughing.
Wait for us, little one!
said Grandpa.
But they could not catch him.
Soon the Gingerbread Man met a Cow in a green field.
Stop, Gingerbread Man!
said Cow.
Come and play with me!
The Cow swished her tail and trotted after him as fast as she could.
But she could not catch him.
Next the Gingerbread Man met a Horse by the fence.
said Horse.
The Horse tossed her mane and galloped after him as fast as she could.
But she could not catch him either.
Then the Gingerbread Man came to a river.
He stopped on the grass, well back from the water.
He could not swim, and he did not know what to do.
Oh dear,
How will I get across?
A friendly Fox with a bushy red tail was sitting on the bank.
I can swim,
said Fox.
Hop on my back, and I will carry you across.
Thank you, Fox,
said Gingerbread Man, and he climbed onto the Fox's back.
The Fox swam across the river.
Splish, splosh, went his paws.
The Gingerbread Man held on tight and stayed nice and dry.
This is fun!
On the far bank the Fox set him down.
There you are,
Where are you running to?
The Gingerbread Man opened his mouth.
Then he shut it again.
He did not know!
He looked back across the river.
Granny, Grandpa, the Cow and the Horse had followed all the way.
Now they stood on the other bank, puffing and waving.
I ran away from everyone who wanted to play with me,
Now I am far away, and I miss them.
Then let's go back,
So the Fox swam back across the river, with the Gingerbread Man on his back.
Will you be my friend, Fox?
I already am,
The Gingerbread Man hopped down and ran to Granny as fast as he could.
Run, run, as fast as you can! You can catch me, I'm the Gingerbread Man!
And Granny caught him in a big, soft cuddle.
I'm sorry I ran away,
We missed you, little one,
That evening Granny and Grandpa sat by the open window with the Gingerbread Man and the Fox.
The Cow and the Horse looked in from the garden.
Granny read them all a bedtime story from her big book, and nobody in the little house was lonely any more.
Goodnight, everybody,
said Gingerbread Man with a yawn.
